Hi Liam / Stratus contracts team,

Attached is the order form we updated to reflect the new quantities (Stratus_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx).

Two asks to help us keep the signature path moving:
- Can your team confirm the commercial fields (list price, effective dates) are OK as marked?
- There are three legal redline items Marissa flagged that we want to align on quickly: (1) data retention carve-out for log exports, (2) SLA credit cap language, (3) termination for convenience notice period. Marissa — I copied you for quick legal take.

If possible, can you return a single redlined doc with tracked comments and a short email confirming any non-material commercial changes? Ben and I will stand by to run this through our legal/finance signoff and generate the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — aiming to have this signed by next Friday to lock the Oct 1 start.

Hi Rachel — thanks for the summary.

We reviewed the draft with our procurement and legal. High level: we accept the capacity numbers and term length, but we've pushed back on two commercial points (billing cadence and an advance notice requirement for burst credits). Legally, we've provided tracked edits to the SLA credit cap and the termination-for-convenience notice (we prefer 90 days instead of 60).

I've attached our redline (returned as Stratus_OrderForm_v3_stratus_redline.docx) — the important sections are labeled with comments. There are also a couple of small clarifications requested on the order form cover (billing contact and tax treatment).

On timing: we can turn this around quickly if we settle the SLA cap language. Our legal says the current proposed cap is below Stratus's risk tolerance. If Redwood can clarify the calculation and add an explicit credits-exhaustion clause, they can greenlight.

-Liam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stratus-systems.com>, contracts@stratus-systems.com
Date: Mon, 09 Sep 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift — order form redlines (legal proposals)

Rachel / Ben —

Thanks for the context and Liam for the returned redlines. I reviewed Stratus's edits and propose the following narrow, final language to resolve the SLA credit cap and termination notice without materially changing Redwood's commercial exposure:

1) SLA credits: replace the current cap language with:
   "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, aggregate SLA credits issued to Customer in any calendar quarter shall not exceed the equivalent of 10% of fees invoiced to Customer for that quarter unless otherwise agreed in writing. Credits shall be applied against future invoices; in the event that Customer has no remaining invoices or the Agreement has terminated, Redwood will issue a one-time cash payment equal to the applicable credit amount. Credits exhaustion: if credits are exhausted under repeated incidents, Redwood will provide a remediation plan and may offer an additional credit at its discretion."

This clarifies the calculation and adds a path for cash payment on termination (Stratus wanted that). It keeps the cap and gives remediation language.

2) Termination for convenience: counterproposal to 90 days — propose 75 days as a middle ground. Suggested wording:
   "Either party may terminate for convenience upon seventy-five (75) days' prior written notice. In the event of such termination, Customer shall pay for services performed up to the effective date and any non-cancellable third-party costs incurred by Redwood in reasonable reliance on the forecasted usage."

3) Data retention carve-out: keep Redwood's standard 90-day log retention but add a limited export window for Customer of 30 days post-termination to pull audit logs (will be provided in CSV format).

Rachel — if Stratus agrees to the above, we can incorporate the edits into a single consolidated tracked document and route for signature. Ben — please confirm if finance can accept Stratus's billing cadence ask (monthly-in-advance vs quarterly). If finance needs to preserve quarterly, flag now so we don't flip-flop in DocuSign.

Happy to take a 20-min call with Stratus legal if they want quick signoff.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0133

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stratus-systems.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift — order form redlines

Marissa — thanks for the thoughtful counters.

Stratus legal is OK with the SLA credit wording so long as the "credits exhaustion" sentence includes a commitment to prioritize mitigation and a timeline for remediation; they asked to add "and Redwood will propose a remediation plan within 10 business days of exhaustion." We've added that small clause in our latest comments.

75 days for termination is acceptable on our side. The data export window is good as-is. On billing cadence, procurement can accept monthly-in-advance (helps our cash forecasting) — we'll confirm final billing contact and tax treatment in the returned document.

If you incorporate the small remediation timeline tweak, we can sign next-day. Please fold all edits into one tracked document and send the DocuSign envelope — we'll expect the final envelope to include the amended order form and the MSA signature page.

I'll stand by for the consolidated file.

Regards,
Liam
